title: Data labeling guidelines scratchpad (asha v6)
content:
High-level: working scratchpad for label guidelines and edge-case triage. Meant for annotators + eng reviewers. Keep short rules + examples.

Goals:
- Reduce labeler disagreement for top-10 ambiguous cases we see in recent audits.
- Capture quick decision rules that are easy to implement in QA checks.
- Provide 10 sample-annotated items per tricky label to share with new contractors.

Quick notes on labels set (current):
- intent: {informational, action, complaint, other}
- pii_present: {yes, no, unsure}
- toxic: {none, mild, severe}
- requires_followup: {yes, no}

Common edge cases + proposed rules:
1) Short polite requests without explicit action ("Could you send the link?")
  - rule: label as intent=action if an explicit request for a follow-up action is present. If phrased hypothetically ("I would like to know"), label informational.
  - examples: 
    * "Could you send the link?" -> intent=action
    * "I would like to know how this works" -> intent=informational

2) System messages / meta-text included in user payloads (e.g., "[system] This is a priority: ...")
  - rule: strip system/meta markers before labeling. If that marker changes interpretation (priority), add tag requires_followup=yes.

3) PII ambiguous cases (initials, job titles, generic locations)
  - rule: mark pii_present=yes only if the snippet contains unique identifiers (full names, SSN, email, phone). Initials or generic city names -> pii_present=no.
  - examples:
    * "John Smith" -> pii_present=yes
    * "J. Smith" -> pii_present=no
    * "San Francisco" -> pii_present=no

4) Sarcasm / rhetorical complaints
  - rule: default to literal interpretation for downstream routing. If labelers suspect sarcasm and it would affect routing (e.g., escalate to CS), add note in comments and set requires_followup=yes.

5) Short contextless fragments (single-word messages: "Thanks", "Now")
  - rule: label as intent=other unless there is clear action word present. Toxic=none unless expletive.

6) Code / stack traces in user text
  - rule: if text is >=40% code-like (backticks, stack traces), set tag "system_text" and intent=other. If user asks a question about the code, label intent=action/informational accordingly.

7) Non-English segments mixed into English (single phrase in Spanish)
  - rule: annotate primary language for pipeline (lang=en/lang=es). For labeling: apply same rules to the translated meaning; add comment "mixed-lang". For now, set requires_followup=yes if translation unclear.

8) Multiple intents in single message ("I need a refund and also how do I change my password?")
  - rule: choose the highest-priority intent for routing: complaints/refund > account action > informational. Record secondary intents in the comment field. If downstream schema supports multi-label, mark both.

9) Free-form profanity vs directed threats
  - rule: mild profanity -> toxic=mild. Threatening language toward an individual or property -> toxic=severe and requires immediate escalation (linked to JIRA-DATA-URGENT in QA checklist).

10) Promotional/advertising content mixed with user query
  - rule: label as intent=other if primary goal is promotion. If there is a genuine question embedded, annotate primary intent as that and tag "contains_advertising".

Annotation examples (samples to include in training set):
- "Please refund my charge from last week" -> {intent: complaint, pii_present: yes (order id), toxic: none, requires_followup: yes}
- "How do I change my password?" -> {intent: action, pii_present: no, toxic: none, requires_followup: no}
- "You're the worst" -> {intent: other, pii_present: no, toxic: mild, requires_followup: no}
- "Error: NullPointerException at line 42
What does this mean?" -> {intent: action, system_text: yes, pii_present: no, requires_followup: no}

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on multi-label schema support (single-column vs multi-column flags). Proposed: keep single primary intent + multi flag columns for secondary intents.
- Need 10 curated examples per edge case (assign to Ryan).
- Add automated QA rule for PII detection threshold (email regex + name heuristics).
- Squad review: schedule 30-min sync with Eng QA and Contract Labeling ops next week.

QA checklist (quick):
- [ ] Add 10 examples for each of the 10 edge cases
- [ ] Update contractor onboarding doc with these decision rules
- [ ] Add unit tests for code-detection heuristic
- [ ] Create JIRA-DATA tickets for top 3 ambiguous rules requiring tooling changes

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep guidance terse — annotators skim. Avoid long paragraphs.
- Add a one-page cheat sheet (one-liner rule + 2 examples).
- Consider adding "confidence" field for annotators to flag uncertain items (low/med/high).

References / links to existing docs: see linked_artifacts above.

Revision history (very short):
- v1: initial notes (Maya)
- v2: consolidated top-5 edge cases (Lee)
- v3: added PII heuristics (Ryan)
- v4: expanded sarcasm rules (Asha)
- v5: sample audits added (contractor batch #9)
- v6: current — streamlined rules and QA checklist (this doc)

End of scratchpad. Will convert to formal doc once we have the 10 example items per case.
